name: How Often to Repaint Exterior Homes in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How often should exterior paint realistically be redone in different Los Angeles County neighborhoods with sun, smog, and coastal exposure?
mainEntity.text: How often should exterior paint realistically be redone in different Los Angeles County neighborhoods with sun, smog, and coastal exposure?

acceptedAnswer.text: General advice that “you should repaint every 7–10 years” ignores how varied Los Angeles County really is. In coastal neighborhoods like Malibu, Redondo Beach, or San Pedro, salt air, fog, and wind-driven rain can shorten a paint job’s life to about 5–7 years, particularly on west- and south-facing walls. In inland valley areas such as the San Fernando or San Gabriel valleys, intense, prolonged sun and high summer temperatures can cause faster fading and chalking, often making 6–9 years more realistic for darker colors. Shadier, more temperate neighborhoods with good overhangs and light colors may see 8–12 years from a high-quality job. Other key factors are surface prep quality (including primer use), the paint line and sheen, and whether previous coats were already failing. Signs you need repainting include widespread chalking, hairline cracking, blistering, or caulk pulling away at joints. Instead of relying on a fixed schedule, inspect your home yearly, focusing on sun-exposed walls, window trims, and fascia. If you see exposed substrate, peeling, or significant fading, you are due. A local painter familiar with your neighborhood’s microclimate can give more precise expectations based on what they see in similar homes nearby.
acceptedAnswer.description: Exterior repaint cycles in Los Angeles County typically range from about 5–7 years in harsh coastal or high-sun zones to 8–12 years in milder, shaded neighborhoods. The true interval depends on sun exposure, coastal salt, smog buildup, surface prep quality, and whether premium exterior paint systems were used.
